draft.title: Should r/LocalLLaMA Consider Moving to a Decentralized Platform Like the Fediverse?
draft.body:
A community member recently raised concerns about the centralization of our current platform, suggesting it might be heading towards what they call 'enshittification' [F1]. They argue that centralized control allows only a few people to dictate how tens or hundreds of thousands communicate, which seems problematic for a community like ours [F2]. Their proposed solution is to migrate to decentralized platforms, specifically the Fediverse, where friendly volunteers could help cover hosting costs [F3][F4][F6]. The author even offers to participate in hosting but doesn’t insist on running their own server [F5].

Given these points, how feasible do you think a migration to the Fediverse or a similar decentralized platform is for r/LocalLLaMA? What challenges might we face regarding moderation, hosting costs, or community engagement? Are there alternative decentralized platforms worth considering? It would be great to hear from those who have experience with decentralized communities or hosting setups. How might we ensure democratic moderation and maintain community cohesion if we move away from centralized platforms?

draft.body:
The suggestion to move r/LocalLLaMA to the Fediverse stems from dissatisfaction with centralized platform control, which some feel concentrates power over communication in the hands of a few [F1][F2]. The source author sees decentralized platforms as the only viable way to address these issues and proposes that community members volunteer to cover hosting costs, with some even willing to help with infrastructure [F3][F4][F5][F6].

What are the practical considerations we should keep in mind if we explore this route? Are there other decentralized platforms besides the Fediverse that might suit our community’s needs better? How can we gauge broader community interest and involvement in hosting or moderation? Opening this discussion seems crucial before any migration decisions are made.
